svg.aria-label: Why the Pi's segments carry 1388 bytes of data and the server's 1440: MSS values, the timestamp option, and MSS clamping

g.text: The server said “MSS 1400” in its SYN-ACK. Every segment also carries 12 bytes of
timestamps (orange), which count against it: 1400 − 12 = 1388 bytes of data.
The Pi said “MSS 1460” (1500 − 40). But on the way out, Bob’s router rewrote it to 1452,
because its internet connection only carries 1,492-byte packets (Chapter 22’s MSS clamping).
So the server sends 1452 − 12 = 1440 bytes of data: packets of exactly 1,492 bytes.

ol.li: Each side tells the other, in its SYN, the biggest segment it can take: its maximum segment size, or MSS, which counts only the data, not the headers. Cloudflare’s servers say 1,400, which leaves room for tunnels along the way. The Pi’s segments are 1,388 bytes.

The capture was taken on the Pi, so it shows the SYN as the Pi sent it. What the server received was different, and the proof is the size of the server’s segments: exactly what fits in Bob’s internet connection. Mystery from Chapter 16, solved from the other side.

figure.figcaption: Why the segments are the sizes they are.
